RaMP multi-database ORA identified Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top pathway with an FDR of 1.39e-12, supported by five input metabolites: 5-HETE (C04805), 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2 (C14717), 15-HETE (C04742), arachidonic acid (C00219), and leukotriene A4 (C00909). The fold enrichment of 1251 reflects a 27-member pathway with all five input compounds as members. Mummichog's m/z-network analysis independently ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top network hit (p=0.00672), capturing the same substrate-to-product lipid cascade including arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. Arachidonic acid is the upstream substrate that branches into the HETE, prostaglandin, and leukotriene arms of eicosanoid synthesis. Methylmalonic acid, L-serine, dehydroascorbic acid, and 6-methylmercaptopurine did not contribute to the eicosanoid pathway hit.
